title: Keep fees on small amount credit contracts within the caps
what: A credit provider may charge on a small amount credit contract only the permitted fees: an establishment fee of at most 20% of the adjusted credit amount and a monthly fee of at most 4%.

laws.title: National Consumer Credit Protection Act 2009 (Schedule 1, National Credit Code)

sources.title: National Consumer Credit Protection Act 2009 (Schedule 1, National Credit Code)
sources.quote: (2) A permitted establishment fee is a fee or charge the amount of which must not exceed 20% of the adjusted credit amount in relation to the small amount credit contract. Maximum amount of permitted monthly fee (3) The amount of a permitted monthly fee that may be imposed or provided for under a small amount credit contract must not exceed 4% of the adjusted credit amount in relation to the contract.

confidence_note: The Code's own words set the caps; they bind only small amount credit contracts.

assessment.summary: A national regime with caps on the cost of small loans replaced differing state caps. The caps protect borrowers but can push smaller lenders out and ration credit to riskier borrowers.

marks.reason: One national regime replaced differing state caps.
Binding caps on fees can ration credit to borrowers whose risk costs more to serve.
Lower allowed margins push some small lenders out.
